title: Impossible Travel Between Presence Pings
dataSources: Life service health (`lifeos:service`), personal scorecards (`lifeos:score`), breach notifications (`hibp:breach`), location visits (`location:visit`), runbook checklists (`runbook:checklist`), and Home Assistant outage events (`homeassistant:event`).
app: Apple and Google location exports, Have I Been Pwned breach alerts, Todoist-style personal runbooks, and Home Assistant outage events streamed into Splunk HEC under `index=personal`.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=location:visit latitude=* longitude=* person=*
| sort 0 person _time
| streamstats current=f last(latitude) as prev_lat last(longitude) as prev_lon last(_time) as prev_time last(city) as prev_city by person
| where isnotnull(prev_lat) AND isnotnull(prev_lon) AND (_time-prev_time)>0
| eval hours_between=round((_time-prev_time)/3600,2)
| eval distance_km=round(sqrt(pow(latitude-prev_lat,2)+pow(longitude-prev_lon,2))*111,1)
| eval implied_kph=round(distance_km/hours_between,1)
| where implied_kph>900
| table _time person prev_city city distance_km hours_between implied_kph
description: Flags jumps between consecutive location events that would require impossible travel speeds for the same person.
value: Impossible-travel logic is a surprisingly useful personal safety and account-takeover signal when location data comes from multiple feeds.
implementation: Normalize phone or location-export data into `location:visit` events with person, city, latitude, and longitude fields.
visualization: Table of impossible travel hops with implied speed and city pair.

references.title: Have I Been Pwned API v3

grandmaExplanation: It watches when your location history says you somehow jumped much too far much too fast to be real.
